Money (Not) to Burn: Payments for Ecosystem Services to Reduce Crop Residue Burning
abstract: We test whether payments for ecosystem services (PES) can curb the highly polluting practice of crop residue burning in India. Standard PES contracts pay participants after verification that they met a proenvironment condition (clearing fields without burning). We randomize paying a portion of the money up front and unconditionally to address liquidity constraints and farmer distrust, which may undermine the standard contract’s effectiveness. Incorporating partial up-front payment into the contract increases compliance by 10 percentage points, which is corroborated by satellite-based burning measurements. The cost per life saved is $3,600–$5,400. The standard PES contract has no effect on burning. (JEL D86, O13, Q12, Q15, Q18, Q53, Q58)
abstract_zh: 我们检验生态系统服务付费（PES）能否遏制印度高污染的秸秆焚烧行为。标准的生态系统服务付费合约，是在核实参与者满足了环保条件（即不焚烧即清理田地）之后才支付报酬。我们随机安排部分款项提前、无条件支付，以应对流动性约束和农户的不信任问题，因为这些问题可能会削弱标准合约的效果。将部分提前支付纳入合约，使合规率提高了10个百分点，卫星遥感测得的焚烧数据也证实了这一结果。每挽救一条生命的成本为3600至5400美元。标准的生态系统服务付费合约对焚烧行为没有任何影响。（JEL D86, O13, Q12, Q15, Q18, Q53, Q58）

title: The Negligible Effect of Free Contraception on Fertility: Experimental Evidence from Burkina Faso

Environmental Externalities and Free-Riding in the Household
abstract: In addition to generating a negative environmental externality, a household’s water consumption entails another “market failure”: household members free-ride off each other and overconsume. The problem stems from consumption being billed at the household level and the difficulty of monitoring one another’s consumption. We document the importance of this phenomenon in urban Zambia by combining utility billing records and randomized person-specific price variation. We derive and empirically confirm the following prediction: Individuals with weaker incentives to conserve under the household’s financial arrangements reduce water use more when their person-specific price increases. Another prediction is that this overconsumption problem is more acute when the financial benefit of a lower utility bill is shared unevenly among household members. We show that households indeed seem more responsive to a change in the household-level price of water when their financial arrangements are more equal. Our results offer a novel explanation for the low price sensitivity of residential water (and electricity) consumption.
abstract_zh: 除了产生负的环境外部性之外，家庭用水还存在另一种“市场失灵”：家庭成员相互搭便车并过度消费。问题源于用水按家庭为单位计费，以及家庭成员之间难以相互监督用水量。我们利用赞比亚城市地区的水费账单记录与随机化的个人层面价格变动，记录了这一现象的重要性。我们推导并通过实证证实了如下预测：在家庭财务安排下节约用水激励较弱的个人，在其个人价格上涨时会更大幅度地减少用水。另一预测是，当水费减少带来的财务收益在家庭成员之间分配不均时，这种过度消费问题会更加严重。我们表明，当家庭的财务安排更为平等时，家庭对家庭层面水价变动的反应确实更为敏感。我们的结果为住宅用水（及用电）消费的低价格弹性提供了一种新的解释。

title: Redesigning Payments for Ecosystem Services to Increase Cost-Effectiveness
abstract: Payments for Ecosystem Services (PES) are a widely used approach to incentivize conservation efforts such as avoided deforestation. Although PES effectiveness has received significant scholarly attention, how PES design modifications can improve program outcomes is less explored. We present findings from a randomized trial in Mexico that tested whether a PES contract that requires enrollees to enroll all of their forest is more effective than the traditional PES contract that allows them to choose which forest parcels to enroll. The modification’s aim is to prevent landowners from enrolling only parcels they planned to conserve anyway while leaving aside other parcels to deforest. We find that the full-enrollment treatment significantly reduces deforestation compared to the traditional contract (41% less deforestation; p = 0.01). As a result, cost-effectiveness of the PES program quadruples. This result highlights the potential to substantially improve the efficacy of conservation payments through simple contract modifications. A randomized trial in Mexico finds that requiring Payments for Ecosystem Services participants to enroll all their forest in the program quadruples cost-effectiveness compared to the standard program design that allows for partial enrollment of land.
abstract_zh: 生态系统服务付费（PES）是一种被广泛采用的激励手段，用以推动避免森林砍伐等保护努力。尽管PES的有效性已受到学界的大量关注，但PES的设计改进如何提升项目成效，则较少有人探讨。我们呈现了一项在墨西哥开展的随机试验的结果，该试验检验了一种要求参与者将其全部森林纳入项目的PES合同，是否比允许其自行选择纳入哪些林地的传统PES合同更为有效。这一改进的目的在于防止土地所有者只纳入其原本就打算保护的地块，而将其他地块留作砍伐。我们发现，全部纳入的处理组相比传统合同显著减少了森林砍伐（减少41%；p = 0.01）。因此，PES项目的成本效益提高了三倍（即变为原来的四倍）。这一结果凸显了通过简单的合同修改大幅提升保护性支付效力的潜力。在墨西哥的一项随机试验发现，要求PES参与者将其全部森林纳入项目，相比允许部分土地纳入的标准项目设计，成本效益可提高至四倍。

The Inherent Trade-Off Between the Environmental and Anti-Poverty Goals of Payments for Ecosystem Services
abstract: Conservation programs in low-income countries often have dual goals of protecting the environment and reducing poverty. This article discusses the tension between these two goals in payments for ecosystem services (PES) programs. Participants who undertake a pro-environment behavior receive a payment, which can be decomposed into two parts: the amount that compensates them for the cost of changing their behavior and the extra amount that is a "pure transfer" to them. To maximize the program's environmental benefits, a policy maker would like to set the pure transfer component to zero, but the pure transfer is the only part of the payment that increases participants' economic well-being. In practice, PES programs pay out some pure transfers, and the extent of the anti-poverty benefits depends on whether the pure transfers are de facto targeted to the poor. I lay out these points and then illustrate them with data from a randomized trial of payments for forest protection in Uganda. I provide evidence that the economic gains from participation in PES are indeed larger for those with low costs to fulfill the program's conservation requirements. I also show that, in this context, poorer eligible households enjoyed more improvement in their economic well-being than richer ones did.
abstract_zh: 低收入国家的保护项目往往兼具保护环境和减少贫困的双重目标。本文探讨了生态系统服务付费（PES）项目中这两个目标之间的张力。参与者若采取有利于环境的行为，即可获得补偿，该补偿可分解为两部分：一部分补偿其改变行为的成本，另一部分则是额外的“纯转移支付”。为使项目的环境效益最大化，政策制定者希望将纯转移支付部分设为零，但纯转移支付却是支付中唯一能够增加参与者经济福利的部分。在实践中，PES项目会支付一部分纯转移支付，而其减贫效果则取决于这些纯转移支付是否事实上瞄准了穷人。我阐明了这些观点，并以乌干达森林保护付费随机试验的数据加以说明。我提供证据表明，对于那些满足项目保护要求成本较低的人，参与PES所带来的经济收益确实更大。我还表明，在这一情境下，较贫困的符合条件的家庭，其经济福利的改善幅度大于较富裕的家庭。

title: Think Globally, Act Globally: Opportunities to Mitigate Greenhouse Gas Emissions in Low- and Middle-Income Countries
abstract: Reductions in greenhouse gas emissions are a global public good, which makes it efficient to act globally when addressing this challenge. We lay out several reasons that high-income countries seeking to mitigate climate change might have greater impact if they invest their resources in opportunities in low- and middle-income countries. Specifically, some of the easiest and cheapest options have already been tapped in high-income countries, land and labor costs are lower in low- and middle-income countries, it is cheaper to build green than to retrofit green, and global targeting matters in integrated economies. We also discuss economic counterarguments such as the challenge of monitoring emissions levels in low- and middle-income countries, ethical considerations, the importance of not double-counting mitigation funding as development aid, and policy steps that might help to realize this opportunity.
abstract_zh: 温室气体减排是一种全球公共物品，因此在应对这一挑战时，全球行动是有效率的。我们阐述了若干理由，说明寻求减缓气候变化的高收入国家，如果将资源投向低收入和中等收入国家的机会，可能会产生更大的影响。具体而言，一些最容易、成本最低的选项在高收入国家已被大量利用；低收入和中等收入国家的土地和劳动力成本更低；建设绿色设施比对现有设施进行绿色改造更便宜；而且在一体化经济中，全球性的精准定位至关重要。我们还讨论了若干经济学上的反对意见，例如监测低收入和中等收入国家排放水平的挑战、伦理考量、避免将减排资金重复计为发展援助的重要性，以及有助于实现这一机会的政策步骤。

title: Using Machine Learning and Qualitative Interviews to Design a Five-Question Survey Module for Women's Agency
How Economic Development Influences the Environment
abstract: Reducing global poverty and addressing climate change and other environmental crises are among the most important challenges facing humanity today. This review article discusses one way in which these problems are intertwined: economic development affects the environment. I synthesize recent microempirical research on the environmental effects of economic development in low- and middle-income countries. The studies that I discuss identify the causal effects of specific aspects of economic development such as greater household purchasing power, expanded access to credit, more secure property rights, technological progress, and stronger regulatory capacity. I conclude by outlining some gaps in the literature.
abstract_zh: 减少全球贫困、应对气候变化以及解决其他环境危机，是当今人类面临的最重要挑战之一。这篇综述文章探讨了这些问题相互交织的一个方面：经济发展影响环境。我综合了近期关于低收入和中等收入国家经济发展对环境影响的微观实证研究。我所讨论的研究识别了经济发展中若干具体方面的因果效应，例如家庭购买力的提高、信贷获取的扩大、更为安全的产权、技术进步以及更强的监管能力。最后，我概述了该文献中的一些空白。

Self-Selection into Payments for Ecosystem Services Programs
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Designers and funders of payments for ecosystem services (PES) programs have long worried that payments flow to landholders who would have conserved forests even without the program, undermining the environmental benefits (“additionality”) and cost-effectiveness of PES. If landholders self-select into PES programs based on how much conservation they were going to undertake anyway, then those who were planning to conserve should always enroll. This paper discusses the less-appreciated fact that enrollment is often based on other factors too. The hassle of signing up or financial costs of enrollment (e.g., purchasing seedlings) can affect who participates in a PES program. These enrollment costs reduce overall take-up, and, importantly, they can also influence the composition of landholders who select into the program—and thereby the program’s environmental benefits per enrollee. Enrollment costs can increase a program’s benefits per enrollee if they are systematically higher for (and thus deter enrollment by) landholders who would have conserved anyway. Alternatively, enrollment costs can dampen per-enrollee benefits if their correlation with status-quo conservation is in the opposite direction. We illustrate these points with evidence from two studies of randomized trials of PES programs aimed at increasing forest cover in Uganda and Malawi. We also discuss how in other sectors, such as social welfare, policy designers have purposefully adjusted the costs of program enrollment to influence the composition of participants and improve cost-effectiveness. We propose that these ideas for targeting could be incorporated into the design of PES programs.
abstract_zh: 生态系统服务付费（PES）项目的设计者和资助者长期以来担心，付费会流向那些即使没有该项目也会保护森林的土地所有者，从而削弱环境效益（“额外性”）和PES的成本效益。如果土地所有者根据其原本就会进行的保护程度进行自我选择，那么原本打算保护的人应当始终会参加项目。本文讨论了一个较少受到重视的事实：参与与否往往还取决于其他因素。报名的麻烦或登记的财务成本（例如购买树苗）会影响谁参与PES项目。这些参与成本会降低总体参与率，而且重要的是，它们还会影响选择加入项目的土地所有者构成，从而影响每位参与者所带来的环境效益。如果参与成本系统性地更高，从而阻碍了那些原本就会进行保护的土地所有者参与，那么参与成本可以提高项目每位参与者的效益。反之，如果参与成本与现状保护行为的相关方向相反，参与成本则可能削弱每位参与者的效益。我们以两项针对乌干达和马拉维森林覆盖率提升而开展的PES随机试验研究为证据，说明上述观点。我们还讨论了在社会福利等其他领域，政策设计者如何有意调整项目参与成本，以影响参与者构成并提高成本效益。我们认为，这些目标瞄准的思路可以被纳入PES项目的设计之中。

title: Cash for Carbon: A Randomized Trial of Payments for Ecosystem Services to Reduce Deforestation
abstract: We evaluated a program of payments for ecosystem services in Uganda that offered forest-owning households annual payments of 70,000 Ugandan shillings per hectare if they conserved their forest. The program was implemented as a randomized controlled trial in 121 villages, 60 of which received the program for 2 years. The primary outcome was the change in land area covered by trees, measured by classifying high-resolution satellite imagery. We found that tree cover declined by 4.2% during the study period in treatment villages, compared to 9.1% in control villages. We found no evidence that enrollees shifted their deforestation to nearby land. We valued the delayed carbon dioxide emissions and found that this program benefit is 2.4 times as large as the program costs.
abstract_zh: 我们评估了乌干达的一项生态系统服务付费项目，该项目向拥有森林的家庭提供补偿：若其保护森林，每公顷每年可获得70,000乌干达先令。该项目以随机对照试验的形式在121个村庄实施，其中60个村庄在两年内获得了该项目。主要结果变量为通过对高分辨率卫星影像进行分类测得的林木覆盖面积变化。我们发现，研究期间处理组村庄的林木覆盖率下降了4.2%，而对照组村庄下降了9.1%。我们没有发现证据表明参与者将其砍伐活动转移到了邻近土地上。我们对延迟排放的二氧化碳进行了估值，发现该项目的收益是其成本的2.4倍。

Liquidity Constraints and Deforestation: The Limitations of Payments for Ecosystem Services
venue: American Economic Review Papers and Proceedings
abstract: A popular environmental policy is to pay forest owners for avoiding deforestation on their land. This is an example of “payments for ecosystem services” (PES). This paper shows that liquidity constraints can limit the effectiveness of PES programs. If an individual would have cut down trees to sell them, his opportunity costs are more front-loaded than the stream of PES income. If credit constrained, he might decline the program even if the net present value (NPV) of the PES income exceeds the NPV of his opportunity costs. I present evidence consistent with this prediction using data on forest owners in Uganda.
abstract_zh: 一项流行的环境政策是向林地所有者支付补偿，以换取其避免砍伐林木。这是“生态系统服务付费”（PES）的一个例子。本文表明，流动性约束可能限制PES项目的有效性。如果某个体原本会砍伐树木以出售木材，那么其机会成本在时间上比PES收入流更为前置。若该个体面临信贷约束，即使PES收入的净现值超过其机会成本的净现值，他仍可能拒绝参与该项目。我利用乌干达林地所有者的数据，提供了与这一预测相一致的证据。

Air Quality and Early-Life Mortality: Evidence from Indonesia's Wildfires
abstract: Smoke from massive wildfires blanketed Indonesia in late 1997. This paper examines the impact that this air pollution (particulate matter) had on fetal, infant, and child mortality. Exploiting the sharp timing and spatial patterns of the pollution and inferring deaths from “missing children” in the 2000 Indonesian Census, I find that the pollution led to 15,600 missing children in Indonesia (1.2 percent of the affected birth cohorts). Prenatal exposure to pollution drives the result. The effect size is much larger in poorer areas, suggesting that differential effects of pollution contribute to the socioeconomic gradient in health.
abstract_zh: 1997年末，大规模野火产生的烟雾笼罩了印度尼西亚。本文考察了这种空气污染（颗粒物）对胎儿、婴儿和儿童死亡率的影响。利用污染在时间上的急剧变化和空间分布特征，并通过2000年印度尼西亚人口普查中的“失踪儿童”推断死亡人数，我发现污染导致印度尼西亚失踪儿童15,600人（占受影响出生队列的1.2%）。产前暴露于污染是这一结果的主要驱动因素。在较贫困地区，效应规模要大得多，这表明污染的差异化影响促成了健康方面的社会经济梯度。
